Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients with signs or symptoms of heart disease.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient has advanced coronary artery disease, multivessel involvement, and ischemic cardiomyopathy, indicating significant heart disease.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients selected because of either medical or research interest to the Principal Investigator.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient's genetic mutation (LDLR) and family history of sudden cardiac death may be relevant for research, but the PI's specific interest is not explicitly stated in the data.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients must not have unstable angina pectoris.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No mention of unstable angina pectoris in the patient's history or current status.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients must not have unstable course following recent (within one month) myocardial infarction.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient's MI history is not recent (multiple prior MI, last MI likely more than one month prior).

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Must not be in New York Heart Association functional class IV heart failure.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient has advanced coronary artery disease and impaired left ventricular function, but NYHA class is not explicitly stated.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: A positive pregnancy test will obviate any cardiovascular testing requiring ionizing radiation.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient is male, so pregnancy status is not applicable.

Recap: Patient has advanced heart disease and a genetic predisposition, but NYHA class IV status is unclear. No evidence of unstable angina or recent MI.
